channel.title: Cybersecurity News
channel.description: Notable but non-breaking cybersecurity news, one finding per item: short summary plus link to the original story.

item.title: Amazon: PHP2Shell exploit attempts started four days before patches shipped
item.description:
Amazon Threat Intelligence says it caught an attempt to exploit the PHP2Shell flaws (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) against its MadPot honeypots on October 17, four days before PHP shipped patches on October 21 and while the bugs were still under embargo. The attempt came from an anonymization-network IP, and it is unclear how the attacker got exploit details early. Several security firms have since reported further exploit attempts after the patches came out, so unpatched PHP 7.x and 8.x servers should be treated as at risk.

Sources: BleepingComputer, The Hacker News

item.title: Microsoft ties ConnectWise Cloud Backup supply chain attack to China-linked Storm-0940 using ARTEX AI agents
item.description:
Microsoft says the China state-aligned actor Storm-0940 was behind the recent compromise of the ConnectWise Cloud Backup app. The group used ARTEX, an agentic AI penetration-testing framework, to automate reconnaissance, password spraying and abuse of the already-consented OAuth app against hundreds of organizations since September 2026. Targets span defense, government, energy, finance, semiconductors, software and more, and the app access let the attackers authenticate without any interactive user sign-in.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: INTERPOL's Operation Serengeti III arrests 1,462 and disrupts 10,909 cybercrime networks in Africa
item.description:
INTERPOL says Operation Serengeti III, run from June 29 to August 31, 2026 across 21 countries, disrupted 10,909 malicious networks, arrested 1,462 suspects and recovered more than $105 million. Investigators identified 65,929 victims and linked the activity to losses above $385 million, with private partners such as Group-IB and Team Cymru supplying intelligence on phishing kits and botnets.

Sources: The Hacker News, BleepingComputer

item.title: Oracle's October 2026 Critical Patch Update fixes 1,209 CVEs, 95 of them critical
item.description:
Oracle's October 2026 CPU ships 1,295 patches for 1,209 unique CVEs, including 95 rated critical and 439 rated high, according to Tenable's analysis. Fusion Middleware got the most fixes (206), and 134 of those can be exploited remotely without authentication. E-Business Suite, Siebel CRM, PeopleSoft, JD Edwards, MySQL and Java SE also received large batches.

Source: SecurityWeek

item.title: QPACK flaws let one unauthenticated connection crash many HTTP/3 servers; three stacks still unpatched
item.description:
FoxIO found QPACK header-expansion bugs in seven of ten HTTP/3 stacks it tested, letting a remote unauthenticated attacker force up to 4,000-fold memory amplification and knock servers offline, and it released working proof-of-concept code. Fixes are out for quic-go (used by Caddy, Traefik and cloudflared), Cloudflare quiche, lsquic and Wireshark, while Bun, the h3 Rust library and aioquic were unpatched at disclosure. The impact is denial of service only, with no attacks seen in the wild.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: CBC: 1.5 million Canadian Crime Stoppers tips exposed in P3 Global Intel hack
item.description:
A CBC investigation found that more than 1.5 million tips submitted to Canadian Crime Stoppers programs over 25 years were exposed in the March 2026 hack of P3 Global Intel, the Navigate360-owned tip platform. About 850,000 records contain personal details such as addresses, phone numbers, emails, licence plates and some banking data tied to cash rewards, and CBC was able to contact more than a dozen tipsters from the data.

The data was stolen by the hacktivist group Internet Yiff Machine as part of a wider leak of more than 8 million P3 records shared with journalists through Distributed Denial of Secrets. Crime Stoppers has not yet detailed the breach scope.

Sources: CBC News, Reuters (March)

item.title: Railway breach exposes customer environment variables, deployments paused
item.description:
Cloud deployment platform Railway says an unauthorized party may have accessed encrypted customer environment variables and, for some, the decrypted contents, which can include API keys and database and registry credentials. Railway ties it to a series of attacks on platform companies aimed at AI inference providers, has paused all deployments, and tells every user to rotate all stored secrets and review logs. Customers are already reporting their keys being used by third parties.

Sources: Railway security disclosure, Railway status page

item.title: PingCAP TiDB Cloud breach: FulcrumSec leaks control-plane, billing and customer API-key data
item.description:
PingCAP confirmed that an attacker used stolen service-account credentials to access its internal cloud systems from September 9 to October 7, copying source code, account and billing records, SQL editor text, and encrypted TiDB Cloud API keys. Extortion group FulcrumSec claims 10.6 TB stolen, including 115K plaintext customer API keys and 180K tenant orgs, and has released 200 GB; PingCAP says it found no evidence customer databases were touched. TiDB Cloud customers should rotate API keys and review access logs.

Sources: Dark Reading, PingCAP incident report

item.title: Japan's Onamae Desktop Cloud hacked, malware on up to 27,000 customer servers
item.description:
Attackers breached the infrastructure of Onamae.com Desktop Cloud, a GMO Internet VPS service popular in Japan for automated FX trading, and installed malware on up to 26,739 customer servers. GMO began shutting down all Desktop Cloud servers at 4 AM local time on October 21 with no restart date, and warns that data on affected servers may be exposed. Customers who stored passwords or other secrets on those servers should rotate them now.

Source: BleepingComputer

item.title: Lazarus uses post-quantum cryptography to deliver malware in FlashHole campaign
item.description:
Kaspersky says North Korea's Lazarus Group is running a campaign it calls FlashHole against South Korean organizations, using the post-quantum ML-KEM-1024 key exchange to protect malware delivery from its command servers. The chain starts with phishing pages pointing to crafted GitHub pages, abuses the INISAFE CrossWeb EX security tool and the Windows fsquirt.exe binary to run shellcode, and pulls more malware from private GitHub repositories. The activity dates back to July 2025.

Source: BleepingComputer

item.title: Critical GitLab flaw (CVSS 10.0) allows unauthenticated RCE on self-managed servers back to 7.0
item.description:
GitLab patched CVE-2026-110264 on October 21, a CVSS 10.0 integer overflow in the bundled Onigmo regex engine that can let an unauthenticated attacker run code on self-managed GitLab servers. Every version back to 7.0 (2014) is affected, and fixes were backported to 18.11.13, 19.0.10, 19.1.9 and 19.2.9 alongside 19.3.6, 19.4.3 and 19.5.1. Instances patched on October 12 are in range again. GitLab reports no exploitation so far and it is not in CISA KEV; GitLab.com and Dedicated are already fixed.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: Ransomware gangs have been exploiting Palo Alto GlobalProtect auth bypass CVE-2026-0257 since June
item.description:
Several ransomware groups are exploiting CVE-2026-0257, an authentication bypass in the PAN-OS GlobalProtect portal and gateway (and Prisma Access) that lets remote, unauthenticated attackers set up an unauthorized VPN connection. Palo Alto patched it in May and first rated it medium severity, but victims now span healthcare, education, government and energy. Unpatched GlobalProtect devices should be updated and checked for unexpected VPN sessions.

Source: Help Net Security

item.title: OVHcloud CLI releases v0.11.0 through v0.15.0 on GitHub were tampered with to steal secrets
item.description:
An attacker used a developer's GitHub account to add an info-stealing binary to OVHcloud's open-source command-line tool, affecting versions v0.11.0 through v0.15.0. The tampered releases were live for about 90 minutes on October 19 before a customer reported them. OVHcloud says v0.16.0 is clean and anyone who downloaded an affected release should update or delete it and rotate secrets on that machine.

Source: Help Net Security

item.title: LiteLLM 1.107.0 on PyPI and Docker shipped a credential stealer and hourly remote code loader
item.description:
All seven wheels of the popular AI gateway library LiteLLM 1.107.0, published to PyPI on October 21, contained malware that runs on every Python start via cook.pth and sitecustomize.py, stealing cloud, SSH, Kubernetes, CI and AI-tool secrets and installing an hourly remote code loader. Docker images tagged v1.107.0, latest, main-latest and main-stable were also affected. PyPI pulled the release; anyone who installed it should treat the host as compromised, rotate every reachable credential and pin to 1.106.2.

Sources: StepSecurity, AISLE, Cyber Security News

item.title: CyberCartel used a multi-model AI agent system to attack 400+ Latin American banks, Straiker reports
item.description:
Straiker documented CARLIY0S, a multi-agent attack system built on the PentAGI framework that the long-running CyberCartel group used against more than 400 Latin American banks and payment providers. It assigned Claude, Grok and Kimi models to reconnaissance, exploit development and target decisions, and Straiker found a stolen-credential database of 4,493 records. It is one of the first detailed looks at criminals running AI-orchestrated intrusions at scale.

Sources: Straiker, Benzinga

item.title: PHP2Shell patches released for critical PHP RCE flaws; exploitation attempts reported in the wild
item.description:
PHP shipped emergency fixes (8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, 8.2.35) for the PHP2Shell runtime flaws CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, which allow unauthenticated RCE on nearly every PHP version back to 5.4. Cloudflare and watchTowr see exploitation attempts in the wild, and governments worldwide issued urgent warnings. This is a material update to yesterday's pre-patch item and is also posted to the breaking feed.

Sources: The Record, The Hacker News, Help Net Security

item.title: Attackers hijacked 300+ Tor exit relays to intercept SSH logins
item.description:
Attackers compromised the Linux hosts behind more than 300 Tor exit relays in early October and rewrote their exit policies to redirect SSH traffic to 12 interception servers that harvested passwords. At the Oct 4 peak the relays carried about 7.5% of Tor's exit capacity; the Tor Project had removed them all by Oct 5. Anyone who logged into SSH with a password over Tor between Oct 1 and 5 and accepted a new host key should rotate that password.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: Stolen UpdraftCentral connection keys used to backdoor WordPress sites after TeamUpdraft breach; up to ~400K sites exposed
item.description:
TeamUpdraft, maker of UpdraftPlus, says attackers breached teamupdraft.com over the weekend of October 17-18 and likely accessed its customer database, including password hashes, 2FA settings and UpdraftCentral, UpdraftVault and UpdraftClone connection keys. Patchstack says attackers began using the stolen keys on October 18 to push at least 99 disguised backdoor plugins and add admin accounts on connected sites, and estimates around 400,000 sites have an UpdraftCentral or Migrator key. Nethemba confirmed malicious plugins on two of its own fully patched sites.

Update UpdraftPlus to 1.26.13 (free) or 2.26.13 (Premium) or later, delete existing UpdraftCentral keys on each site, check for indicators of compromise, and restore from clean backups if compromised.

Source: BleepingComputer

item.title: PHP readies emergency patches for two leaked critical RCE flaws (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) affecting PHP 5 through 8
item.description:
The PHP security team says it will ship emergency updates on Wednesday, October 21 at 7:00 AM PT for two critical vulnerabilities rated 9.2 under CVSS v4.0, after details leaked ahead of the planned embargo. watchTowr says both are remote code execution bugs believed to affect PHP 5, 6, 7 and 8, and that it has reproduced one of them. No exploitation in the wild has been observed yet, and PHP says it may release earlier if details go public or attacks start.

Admins running PHP should be ready to patch as soon as the fixed releases land.

Source: BleepingComputer

item.title: Zeabur shutting down after second breach: leaked plaintext admin credentials exposed 3.2M environment-variable records and 321,810 accounts
item.description:
Developer hosting platform Zeabur is shutting down after its second breach in two months. On October 14-15 an attacker used leaked internal credentials, stored in plaintext and never rotated after the August breach, to get into shared clusters in nine regions, dedicated servers and the production database, stealing about 3.2 million environment-variable records and data on 321,810 accounts. Zeabur also confirmed root sign-ins on 101 GCP servers, SSH keys added to 50 servers, and 16 customer disk copies attached to attacker machines.

Anyone who deployed on Zeabur should rotate every secret, API key and database credential that was stored in its environment variables.

Source: BleepingComputer

item.title: CISA adds the Plex2Shell chain (four Plex Media Server CVEs) to KEV, confirming exploitation
item.description:
CISA added CVE-2026-96652, CVE-2026-96654, CVE-2026-96655 and CVE-2026-96656 in Plex Media Server to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on October 20 (catalog version 2026.10.20). These are the four bugs in the Plex2Shell chain, which lets an attacker go from SSRF with any X-Plex-Token to writing files that run on load. This is an update to the October 18 item, where exploitation had only been reported from a honeypot.

Plex shipped fixes in August; anyone running Plex Media Server older than 1.43.3.10861, especially exposed to the internet, should update now. CISA also added an exploited SiteGuard Server Edition command-injection bug (CVE-2026-106931, covered earlier) and a local Siemens Software Center DLL-loading flaw (CVE-2026-110936) the same day.

Source: CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog

item.title: Mozilla and Chrome confirm private keys for eight eMudhra intermediate CAs were compromised; trust stores rush fixes
item.description:
Mozilla and the Chrome Root Program confirmed on October 20 that the private keys of eight eMudhra (emSign) intermediate CAs, six for TLS and two for code signing, are compromised. Anyone holding them could issue certificates any site would trust. A researcher reported it on October 17, and Chrome and Firefox blocked the keys within hours. No certificates from them had appeared in Certificate Transparency logs before the block, and it is still unknown how the keys left eMudhra or who else holds them.

Mozilla has removed the emSign ECC Root CA - G3 from NSS, and Chrome plans to drop it too. Apple and Microsoft have blocked the certificates, and fixes shipped in Go 1.27.3/1.26.10, Firefox 158.0.1, Python certifi and Rust webpki-roots, while Node.js is still pending. Software that doesn't check revocation needs updating or rebuilding. This confirms the CA behind the urgent Go release reported earlier today.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: Public exploit released for critical unauthenticated FortiSIEM RCE (CVE-2026-106173)
item.description:
Horizon3.ai published a proof-of-concept exploit for CVE-2026-106173 (CVSS 9.4), the FortiSIEM path traversal Fortinet patched last week. An unauthenticated attacker who can reach the gRPC service on TCP port 27918 can combine "../" sequences with a null byte to overwrite a Redis health-check script that cron runs every 60 seconds, turning a file write into code execution.

FortiSIEM 7.5.0 is affected (fixed in 7.5.1 and later) and 7.6 is not. No exploitation has been reported yet, but with a public exploit out, unpatched exposed instances are now at high risk. Source: The Hacker News

item.title: Qilin and INC ransomware gangs exploit PAN-OS GlobalProtect auth bypass (CVE-2026-0257), then pivot to vCenter and ESXi
item.description:
Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 says ransomware crews Qilin (Spikey Scorpius) and INC (Tarnished Scorpius) are still exploiting CVE-2026-0257, a PAN-OS and Prisma Access authentication bypass patched in May and in CISA's KEV catalog since May 13. They use it to set up VPN sessions that skip MFA, then move laterally over RDP and SMB.

In one case the attackers went from the VPN gateway to vCenter, disabled ESXi protections and dumped domain credentials straight from a domain controller's virtual disk, getting around in-guest EDR. Palo Alto urges patching plus a hunt for suspicious gateway-connected events. Source: The Hacker News

item.title: Paradigm Healthcare breach exposed data on 970,000 Medi-Cal members, notified 11 months after intrusion
item.description:
Paradigm Healthcare Services, which handles billing for California's Medi-Cal program, told HHS that an intrusion detected in October 2025 affected more than 970,000 people. Files accessed between Oct 8 and Oct 15, 2025 held names, dates of birth, gender and Medi-Cal member ID numbers.

Notification letters went out Sept 14, 2026, about 11 months after detection. No group has claimed the attack, and Paradigm hasn't said how attackers got in or whether data was exfiltrated. Source: SecurityWeek

item.title: OVHcloud CLI releases v0.11.0 to v0.15.0 backdoored on GitHub to steal developer secrets
item.description:
An attacker hijacked a developer's GitHub account and swapped in info-stealing builds for OVHcloud CLI versions 0.11.0 through 0.15.0, which were live from 14:47 to 16:21 (Paris time) on October 19 before a customer reported them. The malware's goal was to pull secrets off disk. CEO Octave Klaba said release immutability was turned off, so existing releases could be modified without going through CI. Versions 0.10.0 and 0.16.0 are clean, and anyone who installed a bad build should remove it and rotate credentials.

Sources: BleepingComputer, The Hacker News

item.title: Go ships urgent 1.27.3 and 1.26.10 releases that block eight CA intermediate keys, reportedly eMudhra's
item.description:
Go 1.27.3 and 1.26.10, shipped on its URGENT security track on October 20, make Go's certificate verifier reject any chain that passes through eight intermediate CA keys, citing "specific security concerns around their operation." The Go team did not name the CA, but a commenter matched the key hashes to eMudhra emSign intermediates, and Mozilla added six emSign intermediates to its OneCRL blocklist on October 17 through a non-public bug. Go recommends upgrading immediately, and services chained to those keys will fail with an x509 error.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: Russia's APT28 hacked a naval shipbuilder, an aircraft engine maker and police in two NATO countries
item.description:
Symantec attributes a July to September espionage campaign against a naval shipbuilder, a military aircraft engine manufacturer and a law enforcement agency in two unnamed European NATO countries to GRU-linked APT28. The group got in with a malicious Word attachment, used the Hookedge backdoor to steal credentials and map networks, and deployed a new in-memory reflective loader. Researchers couldn't confirm what data was taken, though some intrusions lasted weeks.

Sources: The Record, The Hacker News

item.title: Nikkei discloses third breach in a month; stolen credentials exposed 1.83M records, about 150K with personal data
item.description:
Nikkei Inc., the Japanese business media group that owns the Financial Times, disclosed its third breach in about a month. Attackers used stolen credentials on October 7 to reach a development system and exposed 1.83 million records stored in the cloud, about 150,000 of which include names, email or physical addresses, phone numbers or birth dates. No card data was exposed, and Nikkei says it has no evidence yet of misuse or leaks.

Source: BleepingComputer

item.title: Feds suspect a US ransomware negotiator helped run ShinyHunters' shinywire extortion site
item.description:
KrebsOnSecurity reports that federal investigators suspect an executive at a large US ransomware-negotiation consulting firm took an active role in running shinywire.com, the site ShinyHunters used from about May 3 to October 16, 2026 to pressure nearly 100 victim organizations with private extortion pages. The executive and firm have not been named or charged.

Signal messages seized when Dutch police arrested suspected member Pepijn van der Stap reportedly show negotiators knew of new victims before some victims did. This is separate from Canadian negotiator Edward Dubrovsky, arrested October 8 on sealed cyber extortion charges.

Sources: KrebsOnSecurity, Hackread

item.title: AfD confirms hosting provider hack after hundreds of thousands of internal party emails leak online
item.description:
Germany's AfD party told its state branches that a hosting provider was hacked in September 2026 and that content from individual mailboxes was copied, after a site published what it says are hundreds of thousands of internal emails and documents (a roughly 300 GB dump had been advertised for sale in late September). The party says most affected mailboxes had been inactive for years and current federal-party accounts were not hit.

AfD says it is still checking the authenticity and scope of the published material.

Source: B.Z. Berlin

item.title: Bullhorn takes its staffing platform offline to contain a cyberattack; CrowdStrike assisting
item.description:
Staffing and recruitment software company Bullhorn, which says it serves more than 10,000 customers, disabled access to its platform after detecting a cyber incident that caused a system-wide outage starting Friday. The company says it has isolated the issue and is restoring services after security reviews with CrowdStrike.

Bullhorn says it has not yet determined whether customer data was exfiltrated. ATS/CRM, automation, back office and talent platform services were still in major outage at the time of reporting.

Source: BleepingComputer

item.title: Siemens Software Center DLL flaw (CVE-2026-110936) exploited in ClickFix malware attacks
item.description:
Siemens says attackers exploited CVE-2026-110936, a DLL search-path flaw in Siemens Software Center, by pairing a genuine signed copy of the program with malicious DLLs delivered through ClickFix lures on Windows PCs. Siemens says none of its systems, products or update channels were breached.

Version 4.0.9.8 fixes the issue and installs automatically the next time the app launches. Because the abused file is legitimate, Siemens advises hunting for suspicious behavior and the malware's folders rather than relying on file hashes, and has published indicators of compromise.

Source: SecurityWeek

item.title: GhostAction evolves: GitHub 2FA phishing kit and font-disguised credential stealer found in 94 repositories
item.description:
The GhostAction GitHub supply-chain crew has moved beyond malicious Actions workflows. OpenSourceMalware found a fake GitHub security-alert phishing kit on my-github[.]com that reverse-proxies the login, captures passwords and 2FA codes, and silently authorizes an OAuth device flow with repo and workflow scopes.

The campaign also plants a second-stage credential stealer disguised as a font file that VS Code auto-runs on developer machines and keeps alive with a five-minute cron job, even after the malicious workflow is removed. Researchers found it in 94 repositories belonging to 66 owners, most of them long-abandoned projects.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: One hacker used autonomous AI agents to break into 100+ company websites, including John Deere, SharkNinja and Cummins
item.description:
AI security firm Norforge found a Chinese-speaking attacker using exposed instances of Cairn, an open-source agent orchestration platform, to point autonomous AI agents at more than 1,200 websites, breaching over 100 in the US, Canada, Australia and Japan. Reuters reports the victims include John Deere, SharkNinja and Cummins; successful breaches took about 23 hours each, with the operator giving only short instructions. Deere says there is no sign sensitive data was accessed, SharkNinja says a standalone support site was hit and contained, and Cummins is investigating a third-party vendor site.

Norforge found more than 20 likely malicious Cairn instances and is working to get them taken down.

Source: The Verge (citing Reuters and Norforge)

item.title: Rank Math PRO WordPress SEO plugin compromised in supply-chain attack; v3.0.123 shipped a persistent backdoor
item.description:
Attackers injected malware into some Rank Math PRO 3.0.123 packages distributed between 20:02 UTC on October 15 and 07:12 UTC on October 16 (1:02 PM Oct 15 to 12:12 AM Oct 16 PT). If activated, the malware gives attackers persistent site takeover, recreates a hidden backdoor on each page visit, and can expose credentials, API keys and other secrets. Rank Math pulled the files and released clean version 3.0.124.

Sites that installed and activated 3.0.123 in that window should be treated as compromised and restored from a clean backup taken before the incident. Otherwise, remove the plugin folder and the malicious database entry, block rank1cdn[.]com, and hunt for rogue PHP or .cache files, .htaccess changes, unknown admins, cron jobs and SSH keys.

Source: SecurityWeek

item.title: Citizen Lab: University of Belgrade rector hacked with NSO Pegasus; corruption prosecutor got Apple threat notification
item.description:
Citizen Lab and Serbia's SHARE Foundation found with high confidence that Vladan Đokić, rector of the University of Belgrade and a prominent supporter of the student protest movement, was hacked with NSO Group's Pegasus spyware in 2026. Rade Bajić, a prosecutor who investigated official corruption tied to a failed Belgrade development project, received an Apple threat notification, a strong sign of mercenary spyware targeting. The findings land days before Serbia's October 25 snap election, and the investigations are ongoing.

Source: Citizen Lab report

item.title: Plex2Shell: unauthenticated RCE chain in outdated Plex Media Servers reportedly exploited to drop miners and proxies
item.description:
Plex2Shell chains four Plex Media Server bugs (CVE-2026-96652, -96654, -96655 and -96656) into unauthenticated remote code execution: SSRF steals the owner token, the transcoder writes a payload into the Codecs folder, and the next transcode loads it. Researcher Zach Main published the write-up and proof-of-concept code on October 16, and a honeypot owner reports their internet-facing server was compromised early on October 17 with a crypto miner and a proxy installed. Plex and CISA have not confirmed widespread exploitation.

Versions before 1.43.3.10861 are vulnerable; Plex shipped the fix in August. Update now (pull a fresh image for Docker, check NAS packages by hand), and check older internet-exposed servers for unknown child processes, high CPU, or new files in the Codecs folder.

Sources: Mezha, Zach Main's Plex2Shell write-up

item.title: Hackers exploit critical SiteGuard Server Edition WAF flaw to run commands as root or SYSTEM (CVE-2026-106931)
item.description:
Japanese WAF vendor SiteGuard and JPCERT/CC warn that a critical OS command-injection bug in the statistics feature of SiteGuard Server Edition, which is on by default, is being exploited in the wild and lets attackers run commands as root or SYSTEM. Affected are the Apache httpd, Nginx and IIS editions from 2.20 up to before 8.00 Update 5 (FreeBSD builds before 7.00 Update 6); the vendor says the product protects more than 1.5 million sites. Attackers, victims and scale have not been disclosed.

Patch or apply the vendor's file-replacement fix, which also covers end-of-life versions. Download the diagnostic information from the web management screen first, since remediation may erase attack traces.

Source: BleepingComputer

item.title: Unpatched Broadcom Wi-Fi WPS bug lets nearby attackers take over millions of ISP routers without the password
item.description:
Researcher Quentin Kaiser disclosed at Hexacon in Paris on Oct 16 a memory-corruption bug in Broadcom's proprietary WPS code, present since at least 2010, that gives unauthenticated remote code execution to anyone within Wi-Fi range, without the network key or a completed WPS pairing. He demonstrated root shells on gateways from Proximus, VOO and Orange Belgium, estimates roughly 1.5 million affected devices in Belgium alone, and says none were patched as of Oct 15. Broadcom says it replaced the old code in 2018 but declined to assign a CVE, so many OEMs and ISPs never shipped fixes, and eCos-based chips may never get one.

This is a proximity attack with no reported in-the-wild exploitation, but Kaiser published a fingerprinting script and YARA rule to map affected devices. Turning off WPS where possible and pressing ISPs for firmware updates are the practical steps for now.

Source: Quentin Kaiser's write-up, Hexacon slides

item.title: OpenCode breach exposes stored OpenAI, Anthropic and Google API keys; users report fraudulent charges
item.description:
Anomaly Innovations, the company behind the open-source OpenCode coding agent, emailed affected users on Oct 17 warning that third-party provider keys saved in their workspaces, including OpenAI, Anthropic and Google keys, may have been stolen through a legacy console system it was shutting down. Some users say the keys were already running up unauthorized usage, with reported charges from about $65 to $281, before the warning went out. The company says it hasn't found evidence that other data leaked, and there was no notice on its status page or site at first.

Anyone who stored provider keys in OpenCode should revoke and reissue them directly in each provider's dashboard, check usage and billing logs back to Oct 17, and set spending limits.

Source: Startup Fortune

item.title: ConnectWise Cloud Backup (ex-SkyKick) app credential stolen and used to access Microsoft 365 tenants; Huntress confirms 173
item.description:
Attackers got hold of the Microsoft 365 app credential behind ConnectWise Cloud Backup (formerly SkyKick), a backup service MSPs install with broad access to mailboxes, OneDrive, SharePoint, Teams and directory data. On Oct 15 they scripted Microsoft Graph token grabs across tenants from 144.172.64[.]128, and Huntress has confirmed unauthorized sign-ins in 173 partner and customer tenants. In at least one tenant a separate ConnectWise Teams app gave itself Global Administrator and added credentials to other trusted apps.

ConnectWise has shut down application access for the service, and Microsoft confirmed the activity. Anyone with the app consented should review service principal sign-ins, OAuth grants and app credentials now.

Sources: BleepingComputer, The Hacker News

item.title: ETS hack exposes data on about 7 million California public school students
item.description:
Educational Testing Service, California's statewide testing contractor, says an attacker used a compromised login to copy files from its SFTP site between May 22 and Sept 18, 2026. The data covers all students enrolled in the past three school years, roughly 7 million, including names, birth dates, addresses, disability status, program eligibility and test results. ETS found the activity Sept 25 and began notifying families Oct 16 with two years of Experian identity protection; no SSNs or financial data were involved.

Sources: Los Angeles Times, Politico, California Department of Education notice

item.title: Florida DMV breach exposed driver license and vehicle records, including document images, statewide
item.description:
Florida's Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles (FLHSMV) disclosed on October 16 that an international cybercriminal group got into its driver and vehicle database on September 4 using credentials a Plant City Police Department employee had stored on a personal device. Driver license and motor vehicle data, document images, and other personal information may have been accessed.

The agency says it contained the access and has seen no misuse, but it has not said how many people are affected. Florida Politics reports the attackers set a September 11 deadline to make a deal before leaking the data. Letters are going out to current license and ID holders with a year of free credit monitoring.

Sources: Boca Post, Florida Politics, FLHSMV notice

item.title: Max-severity BlockStrap flaw in Magento and Adobe Commerce lets attackers run PHP code; Sansec expects mass exploitation soon
item.description:
CVE-2026-103849, dubbed BlockStrap, is a template-engine injection in Magento Open Source and Adobe Commerce (through 2.4.9, and B2B through 1.5.3) that lets attacker-controlled email template content execute arbitrary PHP code on store servers. Adobe patched it on October 13 but rated it priority 2.

Sansec says no attacks have been seen yet, but it found four possible attack paths in under a day and expects mass exploitation soon, noting the similar StyleSmuggler flaw went from hotfix to mass attacks in three days. Stores need the October release or Adobe's isolated patch, and should keep the September StyleSmuggler hotfix in place too. Source: bleepingcomputer.com

item.title: Attackers tampered with AOMEI Backupper update servers to push a backdoor to Windows machines
item.description:
Between May and July 2026, attackers repeatedly altered the update and notification config files on AOMEI's own servers for five-to-ten-minute windows, so any AOMEI Backupper install that checked in during a window downloaded and ran a backdoor. Google Threat Intelligence Group, Mandiant and ManageEngine's Threat Analysis Lab disclosed the campaign this week.

The software never cryptographically verified those files, and the checksum sat inside the same unsigned file. AOMEI says its servers are fixed, but that does not clean machines already hit. Source: thehackernews.com

item.title: CISA adds BeyondTrust Remote Support zero-day and Fortinet PEERSTITCH-linked flaw to KEV with Oct 19 deadline
item.description:
CISA added two exploited flaws to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on Oct 16: BeyondTrust Remote Support auth bypass CVE-2026-102764 (BT26-05, exploited by China-nexus actors since August) and Fortinet path traversal CVE-2025-61624 in FortiOS, FortiPAM, FortiProxy and FortiSwitchManager, which surfaced in the PEERSTITCH FortiGate implant campaign.

Both carry a short Oct 19 remediation deadline and CISA's forensic triage requirement. Sources: CISA alert, BeyondTrust BT26-05, Fortinet FG-IR-26-122

item.title: Juniper patches 150+ Junos OS flaws, about two dozen critical; F5 fixes 11 NGINX bugs
item.description:
Juniper Networks published 17 advisories covering more than 150 vulnerabilities in Junos OS and Junos OS Evolved, plus four in Juniper Cloud-Native Router. Roughly two dozen are rated critical and can lead to code or command execution as root, full device takeover, kernel panics, or Routing Engine reboots.

F5 separately fixed 11 NGINX flaws, including critical unauthenticated bugs CVE-2026-15176, CVE-2026-93479 and CVE-2026-97205 that can crash workers or reach RCE if ASLR is disabled or bypassed. Neither vendor reports in-the-wild exploitation. Source: securityweek.com

item.title: Burger King Japan breach exposes about 11.18 million app member records
item.description:
Burger King Japan said a follow-up investigation concluded Oct 13 found unauthorized access between Oct 2 and Oct 7 to the server holding official smartphone-app member data, exposing about 11.18 million customer records. Stolen fields include names, dates of birth, gender, email addresses, phone numbers, and order history; the company says the server did not store credit card numbers and it found no evidence that user credentials were accessed.

Access from the suspicious source was blocked after discovery, the breach was reported to Japan's Personal Information Protection Commission, and no secondary fraudulent use has been confirmed so far. Customers were warned to watch for phishing that impersonates BK Japan. Source: bleepingcomputer.com

item.title: Unit 42 details PEERSTITCH FortiGate implant after FortiManager breach hit 500+ firewalls
item.description:
Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 disclosed PEERSTITCH, a novel memory-resident ARM64 FortiGate implant used in a September 2024 intrusion (CL-STA-0954 / UNC5820) against a telecommunications MSP. Attackers first exploited FortiJump (CVE-2024-47575) on FortiManager, exfiltrating configs, crypto material, and data covering more than 500 managed FortiGate firewalls, then used FortiOS CLI path-traversal CVE-2025-61624 to escalate to root and inject the implant into miglogd and iked.

PEERSTITCH leaves no disk binary, opens no listening ports, and builds a covert inter-process bridge so tagged VPN sessions can bypass FortiOS security checks—hard for conventional EDR/network tools to see. FortiJump and the path-traversal flaw are already patched; defenders should hunt edge appliances for auto-script traversal artifacts, rotate FortiManager-held credentials and keys, and review Unit 42 IOCs. Not a new mass internet zero-day today, but a significant edge-malware disclosure.

Sources: unit42.paloaltonetworks.com; thehackernews.com
